Timber Production
The impacts of coal mining on the timber resource will be of two types: the effect on the area disturbed by mining, and the effect on surrounding forest communities. The impact of removing the forest cover will be long-lasting.
Eventually coal mining activities (including stripping, construction of roads, processing and handling facilities) will completely destroy all vegetation in the areas they occupy. It is estimated that about 25,000 acres of the Project Area will be mined; however, only 80 percent (about 8630 acres) of the forested acreage will be affected by mining. The rate at which this acreage will be mined will vary with the level of production selected. Total years required to deplete the coal reserves varies from 49 to 89 years on Tract II and 56 to 66 years on Tract III, based on maximum and minimum development, respectively. Due to the lengthy time involved in tree growth the difference between the two levels of production in terms of timber production on the forest resources is probably insignificant. However, while the difference in impacts are relatively insignificant for timber (sawlog) production, significantly different impacts may be associated with varying rates of depletion of the forest plant communities which provide wildlife habitat, watershed protection, etc.
